incident-bot: Incident created (1864123456) — autoscale alarm + kv-cache memory blowup in prod-east. Please acknowledge and follow on-call runbook.

maya: acked. alerts started at 03:09UTC — p95/p99 gen latency and token cost spiked. dashboards show continuous_batching average batch_size -> 35 (normal ~8). kv paged block manager metadata count skyrocketed.

ron: i'm on it. any deploys or config changes in the window?

maya: no deploys. config drift check shows no infra PRs. suspicious: a background rollout for a batch-tuning experiment was scheduled but not flagged as deploy.

tara: from node logs (r-infer-09):
```
WARN BlockManager - block_meta leak detected for block_id=blk_0x7fae, live_refs=0, meta_entries=16384
ERROR KVCache - attempted allocate block of 512KB but fragmentation prevented allocation
```

sam: customer impact? kevin-cs — any escalations?

kevin-cs: CS seeing 4 customers with elevated errors (502/504) and 6 with slow responses. One enterprise (acme-corp) opened a ticket, reported timeouts in chat completions. We'll notify customers that we're investigating and will follow up in 30m.

ron: initial hypothesis: background experiment increased continuous_batch_window_ms and indirectly allowed bigger batch growth, which drove prefix/KV cache churn and excessive small-block allocations. That + block manager eviction policy didn't keep up -> metadata blowup.

maya: metrics: prefix cache hitrate dropped 18% after 03:05UTC, KV metadata entries doubled in 2 minutes. GC cycles increased and I/O waits spiked.

ops-bot: recommended mitigation from runbook: 1) reduce continuous_batch_window_ms to baseline, 2) tighten max_batch_tokens, 3) trigger blockmanager evict sweep.

ron: let's apply hotfix: reduce continuous_batch_window_ms from 50 -> 12ms and set max_batch_tokens from 8192 -> 2048 on prod-east routing policy. I'll push a config patch to the control plane now.

maya: rolling patch command used:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/v1/configs/policy/prod-east" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"continuous_batch_window_ms":12, "max_batch_tokens":2048}'
```

ops-bot: change accepted; config propagated to 12/15 inference nodes in prod-east; last node will pick up in ~20s.

tara: after the change — observed immediate drop in avg batch_size to ~10, KV metadata growth slowed. however metadata count still high on nodes r-infer-08/09. recommending a targeted evict and blockmgr compact on those nodes.

sam: can we evict/purge safely? any risk to in-flight responses?

ron: we have an internal safe-evict command that waits for KV refs to drain. plan: run `blockmgr compact --node r-infer-08 --mode staggered --grace 30s`. I'll run on 08, then 09.

maya: running now on r-infer-08. logs: `compact started, freed 1.2GB metadata, reclaimed 320 blocks`.

rita (ops-bot): healthcheck: r-infer-08 OK, p99 latency down 45%.

ron: compact on r-infer-09 next. will run staggered to avoid cluster-wide perf impact.

(10m pass)

kevin-cs: customers updated. acme-corp still sees occasional slow requests but overall improved. they appreciate the update.

tara: after compacts, metadata counters returned near baseline. we still see elevated fragmentation in block sizes; block allocations show many small allocations (~4-8KB) causing fragmentation overhead.

sam: root-cause note: combination of an experimental batch scheduling change + a subtle bug in block manager's allocation heuristic that fails to coalesce small free regions quickly. The bug manifests under large, bursty batch growth.

ron: immediate actions (hotfix/mitigation):
- reverted experimental batch rollout and forced baseline policy in prod-east (done).
- lowered continuous_batch_window_ms and max_batch_tokens (done).
- ran targeted blockmgr compactions on affected nodes (done).
- opened a temporary routing fallback to smaller models if nodes cross memory threshold (enabled).

maya: post-mitigation metrics: kv metadata delta back to normal in ~12 minutes; p99 gen latency back within SLOs for all but 1 customer who needed a dedicated retry. No data loss.

kevin-cs: customer communications sent: interim status, ETA for full mitigation, offer for dedicated support if needed.

ron: medium-term fixes:
- block manager: improve coalescing and free-list compaction (PR created #3592).
- allocation heuristic: avoid allocating many tiny blocks when batch influx detected (PR #3593).
- add telemetry that correlates batch_size distribution with block allocation sizes (task assigned).

tara: follow-up ops items:
- add alert for metadata_count/growth rate (was missing).
- add canary check for experimental batch rollouts to prevent uncontrolled ramp.
- add a safemode for blockmgr when metadata_count > threshold to reject new block allocations and fall back to streaming path.

ron: owner assignments — please ack:
- PR #3592 blockmgr coalesce fix -> tara (owner)
- PR #3593 allocation heuristic -> ron (owner)
- Telemetry + alert -> maya (owner)
- Customer follow-ups -> kevin-cs (owner)

maya: all acked. I'll start the alert + telemetry ticket after this thread.

incident-bot: Incident 1864123456 mitigated (status: partial). Postmortem required; severity: SEV2. Please create postmortem doc and link it here within 48h.

kevin-cs: will draft customer-facing summary for legal/comms.

ron: leaving notes for on-call handoff: if metadata_count rises > 3x baseline, trigger staged compaction and roll back batch policies immediately. Handing to night on-call @sam.

sam: thanks — I'm up. I've got runbook and will monitor for 2h.

(End of thread)
